Search this repository (/bench/repo) to answer two things:

1. Is there any GraphQL schema anywhere? Look for files like *.graphql, *.gql, schema definitions, references to "graphql", "typeDefs", "buildSchema", apollo, etc. Report exact file paths if found, or state definitively that there is no GraphQL.

2. What IS the actual public API surface of this repo? Look for REST endpoints, RPC, OpenAPI/Swagger specs, route definitions, API handlers, tRPC, etc. Identify how the public/external API is defined and where. Give concrete file paths and a short description of the API style.

Be thorough — check the project structure, package.json / config files, and any api/ or server/ directories. Report file paths for everything you cite.

attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text:
I have a complete and definitive picture. Here are my findings.

## 1. GraphQL: None. Definitively absent.

This repo (the **Memos** project — an open-source, self-hosted note-taking tool, Go backend + React/TS frontend) contains **no GraphQL of any kind**:

- No `*.graphql` or `*.gql` files exist anywhere.
- No references to `graphql`, `typeDefs`, `buildSchema`, `apollo`, `urql`, or `relay` (as a GraphQL library) in any source, config, or lockfile.
- The only two grep hits were **false positives**: `web/src/components/ColumnGrid/ColumnGrid.tsx` matched on the word "relayout"/"Relayouts" (a masonry layout function, not GraphQL Relay), and `web/pnpm-lock.yaml` matched the same "relay" substring. No `graphql` string appears in either.

The API is defined via Protobuf/gRPC, not a schema-definition language like GraphQL.

## 2. Actual public API surface: Protobuf-first, multi-protocol (gRPC + Connect + REST/gRPC-Gateway), plus OpenAPI, RSS, and MCP.

The single source of truth is **Protobuf service definitions**, from which gRPC, Connect-RPC, REST, and an OpenAPI spec are all generated.

**Source of truth — Protobuf service definitions** (`proto/api/v1/`):
- `proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto`
- `proto/api/v1/user_service.proto`
- `proto/api/v1/auth_service.proto`
- `proto/api/v1/attachment_service.proto`
- `proto/api/v1/shortcut_service.proto`
- `proto/api/v1/instance_service.proto`
- `proto/api/v1/idp_service.proto`
- `proto/api/v1/ai_service.proto`
- `proto/api/v1/common.proto`

Each RPC carries a `google.api.http` annotation defining its REST mapping (e.g. `GET /api/v1/memos`, `GET /api/v1/{name=memos/*}`, `POST /api/v1/auth/signin`, `GET /api/v1/auth/me`). The API design explicitly follows Google AIP guidelines (`proto/api/v1/README.md`). Codegen is driven by `buf` (`proto/buf.yaml`, `proto/buf.gen.yaml`).

**Generated code** (`proto/gen/`):
- gRPC stubs + gRPC-Gateway: `proto/gen/api/v1/*_grpc.pb.go`, `proto/gen/api/v1/*.pb.gw.go`
- Connect-RPC handlers: `proto/gen/api/v1/apiv1connect/*.connect.go`
- OpenAPI 3.0.3 spec: `proto/gen/openapi.yaml` (embedded into the Go binary via `proto/openapi_embed.go` → `proto.OpenAPIYAML()`)

**Server-side handler implementations** (`server/router/api/v1/`) — business logic for each service, e.g. `memo_service.go`, `user_service.go`, `auth_service.go`, `attachment_service.go`, `shortcut_service.go`, `instance_service.go`, `idp_service.go`, `ai_service.go`, `reaction_service.go`, `memo_share_service.go`. Key wiring files:
- `server/router/api/v1/v1.go` — `APIV1Service`, embeds the generated `Unimplemented*Server` types; `RegisterGateway` mounts gRPC-Gateway + Connect handlers on the Echo server with a shared authorizer.
- `server/router/api/v1/connect_handler.go` — `ConnectServiceHandler` registers all 8 services as Connect handlers on an `http.ServeMux`.
- `server/router/api/v1/connect_services.go` — Connect method wrappers delegating to the gRPC implementations (single source of business logic serving both gRPC and Connect protocols).
- `server/router/api/v1/authz.go`, `connect_interceptors.go`, `acl_config.go` — auth/ACL.

**Top-level HTTP mounting** (`server/server.go`) — an **Echo** HTTP server mounts everything:
- `GET /healthz` health check (also `server/router/api/v1/health_service.go`)
- Frontend static files: `server/router/frontend/frontend.go`
- File server (attachments/blobs): `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`
- RSS feeds: `server/router/rss/rss.go`
- gRPC-Gateway REST + Connect API under `/api/v1/...` via `apiV1Service.RegisterGateway`
- SSE (server-sent events) endpoint: `server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go`, `sse_hub.go`, `sse_event_helpers.go`

**MCP server** (`server/router/mcp/`) — an additional public surface at `/mcp` (Model Context Protocol, Streamable HTTP transport). It is **OpenAPI-driven**: it reads the embedded `proto/gen/openapi.yaml`, indexes operations by `operationId`, and translates MCP tool calls into in-process `/api/v1/...` REST requests. Key files: `service.go`, `openapi.go`, `catalog.go`, `adapter.go`, plus `README.md`.

### API style summary
**Protobuf/gRPC-first, exposed over four coordinated surfaces:** (1) native **gRPC**, (2) **Connect-RPC**, (3) **RESTful JSON** over `/api/v1/...` via gRPC-Gateway (with resource-oriented, AIP-style paths), and (4) an auto-generated **OpenAPI 3.0** spec. On top of that, the server also exposes **RSS** feeds and an **MCP** endpoint (`/mcp`) that reuses the REST API. There is **no GraphQL, no tRPC, and no hand-written Swagger** — the OpenAPI doc is generated from the proto definitions. The README confirms this: "full REST and gRPC APIs for integration."
